valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E (FY2027 adjusted EPS per ADS viewed at the Nov 2027 target date). Integrated oil and gas, mid-cycle judgement. ADR ratio 1 ADS = 1 ordinary share, and Equinor reports in USD, so no FX conversion is needed. Anchor: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS $1.20 (adjusted net income $2.86B) and a $0.39 quarterly dividend, from the Oct 28 2026 release. FY2027 EPS and multiples are our stated assumptions, not a sourced forecast.

bear.driver: Oil and gas prices fall back from the 2026 spike, so earnings fall well below the Q3 run-rate.

base.driver: Prices ease but stay above 2025; production growth and buybacks (up to $3B in 2026) support per-share earnings.

bull.driver: Elevated commodity prices persist and output guidance is raised again.

valuation.implied_by_close: At base EPS $4.20 the close implies 10.2x; the sampled TD Cowen $38 target implies 9.0x, or EPS $4.00 at 9.5x
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $4.20 (9.8 pp of the close)
valuation.watch_metric: Adjusted EPS per share and realised liquids and gas prices against the $1.20 Q3 level
valuation.next_disclosure: Equinor fourth quarter 2026 results, expected early February 2027 (date not confirmed)

analyst_notes: Only a small named sample was found (TD Cowen, Morgan Stanley, Santander), and the targets are mostly stale. TD Cowen's $38 Hold target sits below the close and implies about 9.0x our base EPS; its target moved between $37 and $42 from May to July. Published consensus is Hold with a target near $39-41. Q3 adjusted EPS of $1.20 missed a $1.37 consensus reported by one outlet, and calls after the Oct 28 release were not verified.
